findings.statement: Round 1 F-1 is closed on the path side, but the same false marker now decides the event's project on the cwd side. Delta REQ-ENF-004 defines the project as "the nearest ancestor of `cwd` (including `cwd` itself) with `.warrant/warrant.json`". The same text also says that a call whose `cwd` is in another checkout is judged by that checkout, while a path of another checkout inside the project directory is a path of this project. The repository already contains `packs/core-sdd/golden/{chore,factory-change,feature}/.warrant/warrant.json`. These are directories of the same checkout, not checkouts. Suppose an agent with an active `implement` Run in the main checkout does `cd packs/core-sdd/golden/feature`, for example to look at the golden output. By the checkout reading, the event is judged by the main checkout: its Run, its `write_scope` and `deny` (SCN-ENF-011). By the literal "nearest warrant.json" reading, the project becomes the golden directory, the main checkout's Run is not visible, and an edit of `<main>/packages/cli/src/**` by absolute path counts as outside the project: `allow`, with no event in `guard_events[]`. An agent can also create the marker itself (`mkdir -p x/.warrant && echo {} > x/.warrant/warrant.json && cd x`). The shell is not restricted outside a `review` Run. If the file has invalid content, policy does not load, but an edit with no project path is decided before policy loads (`allow`). design D2 rejects exactly this marker ("The marker is false ... The agent creates it itself and moves paths out of `write_scope`"), and D1 uses it for `cwd`. The result is class A (ADR-0048 item 2), the very class this Change is meant to close.
findings.recommendation: Make the event-root marker an observable property of a checkout, not just of `.warrant/warrant.json`. For example: `.warrant/warrant.json` plus a `.git` entry (file or directory; for a git worktree `.git` is a file) in the same directory. Alternatively, go up from `cwd` to the nearest such checkout and only then to `.warrant/warrant.json`. State explicitly that a directory with only `.warrant/warrant.json` (golden, fixtures, one created by the agent) is part of the enclosing project. Add a scenario: an active `implement` Run in the process directory, event `cwd` = `packs/core-sdd/golden/feature` (`.warrant/warrant.json` without `.git`), edit of `src/app.ts` of the main project by absolute path outside `write_scope` gives `deny`, and the event is written to that Run.

findings.statement: The spec does not describe edits from a worktree session to paths of the enclosing (main) checkout. A git worktree lies inside the main checkout (`<main>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`). After D1 the event's project is the worktree, so the path `<main>/packages/cli/src/a.ts` is outside the project: `allow`, and it is not written to `guard_events[].paths` (except under a `review` Run). Today (the process directory is the main checkout, per A-1) the same edit is judged by the main checkout: without a Run it is `deny` with hint `run start` for `paths.src` and policy paths; with a Run it is checked against `write_scope`. An agent mistakenly writing to the original checkout instead of the worktree is a typical class A error for LATTICE (proposal Why). The Change weakens this case, and neither proposal, design nor the scenarios mention it. D2 covers only the reverse direction (main session -> worktree file). SCN-ENF-057 covers only `cwd` outside all projects.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly how to judge a path outside the event's project that lies in another project under WARRANT: the process-directory project or a project containing the event root (see decisions_required D-1). Either `deny` with a hint to edit inside your own checkout, or judge it by that project (its policy and Run), or accept `allow` as a limit, written in the norm. Add the case to SCN-ENF-056: an edit of a main-checkout `src/**` path from a worktree `cwd`, with the decision and the event write.

findings.statement: The `cd` rule under a `review` Run (delta REQ-ENF-004) allows `cd` to a path inside the event's project. It justifies `deny` otherwise like this: "`run finish` and `run submit` without a Run id act on the Run of the checkout `cd` leads to". D2 and the new sentence of the norm ("a path of another checkout inside the project directory is a path of this project") make a nested git worktree part of the project. So `cd .claude/worktrees/<name> && warrant run finish --state CANCELLED` and `cd .claude/worktrees/<name> && warrant run submit --file e.json` under a `review` Run of the main checkout are `allow`. The CLI does not walk up ("the CLI does not go up", `commands/context.ts`), so they act on the worktree's Run, which is a different checkout. That is exactly the effect the rule is meant to prevent. A read-only Run cancels another session's Run. Round 1 F-8 asked for `deny` of this case. I-1 closes F-8 by D2, but D2 is about edit paths, not about which checkout `warrant run …` runs in.
findings.recommendation: For `cd`, require not only "inside the project" but also that the target directory and its ancestors up to the project root have no other checkout (`.warrant/warrant.json` with `.git`, per the F-1 marker). Otherwise `deny` with the same hint. Add to SCN-ENF-044: `["bash", "-c", "cd .claude/worktrees/w && warrant run finish --state CANCELLED"]` (`w` is a nested checkout under WARRANT) gives `deny`.

findings.statement: proposal: "For `--frontend claude` the same: the `cwd` of the native input". But REQ-ENF-005 is not in the delta, and it still requires code 2 for "input that cannot be parsed", with no exception. Delta REQ-ENF-004 and SCN-ENF-016 now say: "input that does not parse as an event is judged in the process directory", and when that directory is not under WARRANT the result is `allow`. Today the adapter checks `underWarrant(ctx.root)` before parsing (design Context), so in a directory without WARRANT a non-JSON input gives empty stdout and code 0. D1 changes the order to parse first, then find the root. For `--frontend claude` with a process directory not under WARRANT and a non-JSON input there are two readings: code 2 with stderr (REQ-ENF-005, SCN-ENF-021) or `allow`/code 0 (SCN-ENF-016). For Claude Code this is an observable difference: the action is cancelled or not. The same applies to native JSON without `cwd`. Round 1 F-6 raised this point, and I-1 closed it only for the form without `--frontend`.
findings.recommendation: Add REQ-ENF-005 to the delta (MODIFIED). State that the project of the native input is found from its `cwd` by the REQ-ENF-004 rule. A native input that does not parse, or has no `cwd`, is judged in the process directory: not under WARRANT means empty stdout and code 0; otherwise code 2 as before. Add that case to SCN-ENF-021 or SCN-ENF-016.

findings.statement: No scenario covers the case where the process directory is not under WARRANT and the event `cwd` lies in a project. The norm (root by `cwd`, fallback to the process directory) says it is judged by the event's project. design D1 says: "if the input did not parse, the process directory is checked, as now: when that directory is not under WARRANT the input is not read". The second half can be read as "underWarrant(process) is checked before reading the input", which gives `allow` without reading. SCN-ENF-056 fixes only a process directory that is a project, and SCN-ENF-016 only a process directory not under WARRANT with no project at `cwd`.
findings.recommendation: Add to SCN-ENF-056 (or a new scenario) the case of a process directory without `.warrant/warrant.json` and an event `cwd` in a project with a `RUNNING` Run: an edit outside `write_scope` gives `deny`, and the event is in that project's Run. In D1, rephrase "the input is not read" as "a non-parsing input in a process directory not under WARRANT gives `allow`".

findings.statement: SCN-ENF-057: "an edit of its path outside `write_scope` gives `deny`". It does not say that the path must be absolute. Event paths are resolved from `cwd` (REQ-ENF-004), and `cwd` here is outside all projects. A relative path like `docs/readme.md` resolves outside the process project and gives `allow` with no event. The scenario has two readings, and the test may pick the wrong one.
findings.recommendation: Write in SCN-ENF-057 that the path is absolute (`<process project>/docs/readme.md`). Add the relative path `docs/readme.md` as a second case: outside the project, `allow`, the event's `paths` empty.

findings.statement: proposal Why states as a fact: "Claude Code runs the hooks of a worktree session from the main checkout. This shows in the SessionStart hook". But `brief.js` takes its root from `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` first, so naming the main checkout does not tell apart the process directory and `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. design rightly treats this as assumption A-1, and the probe goes into the backlog after the release (task 2.2). So 0.10.1 ships to LATTICE without proof that it fixes #138. D1 does no harm if A-1 is wrong (design), but it does not help either. Also, round 1 F-4 is closed by accepting it as a limit ("a call from another checkout is judged by that checkout, a limit like INV-07"). Yet the D2 argument against the rejected option ("`cd` into the main checkout would move paths out of the worktree Run's `write_scope`") applies equally to the chosen D2. After `cd` into the main checkout, a worktree path is judged by the main checkout's policy, where `.claude/worktrees/<name>/…` matches neither `paths.src` nor the worktree Run's `write_scope`.
findings.recommendation: In proposal, say "apparently" or reference A-1. Run the probe before the 0.10.1 release, not after. In D2, remove the `cd` argument from the rejection reasons of the "outside the project" option, or state that the chosen option has the same limit.

unknowns.question: Does Claude Code's hook input `cwd` follow `cd` in the session's Bash tool (is the current shell directory persisted into later PreToolUse/PostToolUse events)? F-1 and F-2 depend on this: with persistence, the project switches with a single `cd` by the agent.

assumptions.statement: I did not check the guard code (`core/guard/guard.ts`, `commands/guard.ts`, `bin/warrant.ts`). In the review Run, code search via Grep is denied by the hook and shell is restricted. The order of `underWarrant` and input parsing, and the root of the `warrant` CLI (`process.cwd()`, no walking up), are taken from design Context.

`paths.src` and the `match.paths` of the `factory-change` profile are taken relative to the project root. So a main-checkout path `.claude/worktrees/<name>/packages/cli/src/**` does not match `packages/cli/src/**` (basis of F-7).

decisions_required.question: How should guard judge an edit of a path outside the event's project that lies in another project under WARRANT: the process directory or the checkout that contains the event's worktree (F-2)?
options: allow, as for any path outside the project: accept as a limit in the norm and in SCN-ENF-056
deny with a hint to edit inside your own checkout (`cwd`)
judge by that project: its policy and active Run, with the event written to its Run

decisions_required.question: What marks the event's project when going up from `cwd` (F-1)?
options: `.warrant/warrant.json` plus `.git` (file or directory) in the same directory
the nearest git checkout (`.git`), then `.warrant/warrant.json` at its root
`.warrant/warrant.json` only (current text), accepting the golden directories and self-created markers
